chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman inherits from the bricks and does not inherit anything from the land.' I said, 'How is it that she inherits from the branches and does not inherit anything from the roots?' So he said to me: 'There is no lineage for her from them by which she inherits. Rather, she is an outsider to them, so she inherits from the branches and does not inherit from the roots, and an outsider is not included upon them by reason of her.'

key_terms.الْأَصْلِ: the root (metaphor for the land itself)

ai.seo_question: Why does a woman inherit from the bricks but not the land in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the juristic distinction between inheriting the superstructure (buildings/bricks) versus the land (root) for women, emphasizing that their lineage connection is through the male line, making them 'outsiders' to the paternal estate's core. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle that inheritance rights are strictly tied to nasab (lineage), where the woman inherits the value of the improvements she or her husband's line contributed, but does not transfer the land ownership to her own descendants through her. The Imam clarifies that no 'outsider' enters the paternal lineage through her, reinforcing the patrilineal nature of property transmission in this specific context.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman (widow) does inherit from the bricks and does not inherit anything from the land’. I said, ‘How comes she inherits from the branches and does not inherit anything from the roots?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘There is no lineage for her from them to inherit by. But rather, she has entered (from being an outsider) upon them, so she inherits from the branches and does not inherit from the roots, and an outsider is not to be included upon them by the cause of it’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘A woman inherits from bricks but does not inherit from residence anything.’ I then asked, ‘How is it that she inherits from branches but not from the roots?’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘She does not have lineage because of which she can inherit. She is an addition to them thus she inherits from branches and not from the roots and no addition is made to them because of her.’”
